races.name: Thank You GRP Solutions For Sponsoring Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Chasing Time
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced type with strong OR 120 rating represents in-form Charlie Appleby stable (1/9 last 14 days), but unknown running style creates tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Sinocentric
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 24-day break needs pace to aim at, but David Simcock's 0/4 recent record suggests stable not firing.

runners_data.name: Killer Whale
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning from 115-day break with Andrew Balding (8/29 strike rate) and proven on similar going, ideal to control this small field.

races.paceDynamic: Killer Whale is the only natural front runner in this three-horse field and will dictate terms from the front without pressure. Rob Hornby can set a controlled, measured gallop over this stamina-testing 1m4f trip, with Sinocentric tracking from midfield and the lightly-raced Chasing Time yet to show his preferred position. The lack of pace pressure means the leader won't soften up, while the small field reduces the usual advantage hold-up horses gain from cover and splits. This setup strongly favours prominent runners and the pace-setter — there's insufficient pace to string out the field and create the scenario hold-up horses need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Killer Whale gets an uncontested lead and dictates the gallop.
scenarios.body: Rob Hornby can dictate fractions without pressure, saving energy for a sustained finish that the 115-day break will have freshened him for. The prominent position proves decisive when there's no genuine pace to expose him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Charlie Appleby Quality
scenarios.trigger: If Chasing Time shows the class that his OR 120 rating suggests despite limited experience.
scenarios.body: The Godolphin runner's superior official rating reflects genuine ability, and Billy Loughnane's booking suggests stable confidence in this lightly-raced type. Charlie Appleby's 1/9 record in the last 14 days indicates the stable is in form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Sinocentric and Chasing Time both track Killer Whale closely, creating more pressure.
scenarios.body: The increased pace favours Luke Morris on Sinocentric, whose hold-up style benefits from a stronger gallop to aim at. David Simcock's runner gets the run of the race from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all three runners go steady early and it becomes a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace throughout means stamina becomes less important and speed takes over in the final furlong. This neutralizes the distance advantage and makes it a lottery finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch for any early move from Chasing Time - if Billy Loughnane sends him forward early, it suggests they want to use his class advantage.
Monitor Killer Whale's jump from the stalls after the long break - any sluggish start could compromise his front-running tactics.
Observe if Sinocentric gets cover in the small field - Luke Morris needs to find a position to launch from in the straight.
Track the early fractions - if they go too steady, it becomes a sprint finish that could upset the form book.

races.name: In Remembrance Of Aggrey Burke Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Poetic Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been in good form lately with a recent win, but 12-year-old veteran may lack pace for sprint finish

runners_data.name: Yehudi
runners_data.note: Only front-runner in field gives him tactical advantage, but inexperienced 7lb claimer Hope Regan may not maximize this edge

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who caught stewards' attention last time, suggesting trainer James Owen struggling to get tune right
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in two 7f runs for new yard; down in weights; first run over further than 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins over 6f for previous trainers; unplaced in two runs for new stable (7f), catching the attention of the stewards on the first occasion, and hopes appear to rest on this first attempt at further than 7f having a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Coloane
runners_data.note: Showed promising return from 108-day break last time, valuable 3lb claimer Whiteley can help her competitive weight
runners_data.comment: Promising run after a break here two weeks ago; shouldn't be too far away
runners_data.spotlight: Infrequent winner but she made a promising return from a 108-day break here two weeks ago; talented claimer takes off a valuable 3lb; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse who hung badly when winning chance arose in February, raising questions about his resolution
runners_data.comment: Second over C&D in February, when rather throwing the race away; not so good twice since
runners_data.spotlight: Hung away a winning opportunity over C&D in February and neither run since has been as good; more minor money perhaps his best hope.

runners_data.name: Always Fearless
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse in good form with recent win, proven at this trip and effective in sprint finishes

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 37 days since last run may have dulled his edge, better over longer distances

runners_data.name: Nala The Lioness
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated hold-up horse in field, 25 days off and poor recent form makes her hard to fancy

races.paceDynamic: Yehudi is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable gallop without pressure from the start. The entire field behind him consists of hold-up horses who will be content to settle in the back half of the field. This creates a slow early pace that will build into a sprint finish over the final 3f as the hold-up brigade all try to unleash their finishing kicks simultaneously. This setup strongly favours horses with the best turn of foot — those who can produce the most devastating late surge when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi sets an uncontested lead and the hold-up horses all come late together.
scenarios.body: The pace will be pedestrian for 6f before exploding into a cavalry charge home. Horses with the best finishing speed like Always Fearless and Coloane can unleash their strongest asset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Yehudi Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi gets such a soft lead that he can quicken clear before the closers get organized.
scenarios.body: The favourite's prominent style pays dividends if he can build an unassailable advantage. Hold-up horses left with too much to do in a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses all converge at once and create interference in the straight.
scenarios.body: Several horses will get stopped in their tracks or forced to switch wide. The clearest passage determines the winner more than pure ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Leader Folds
scenarios.trigger: If Yehudi fails to handle the step up in trip and fades from halfway.
scenarios.body: An even more pedestrian pace as the field concertinas together. The horse who can quicken latest wins in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Yehudi must be watched closely early - if 7lb claimer Hope Regan lets him bowl along too fast he'll empty out
Traffic problems are inevitable with seven hold-up horses converging in the straight - watch for interference
Always Fearless has won recently but check if the 9-year-old veteran can reproduce that effort again so soon
Coloane's return to form last time was eye-catching - monitor if 3lb claimer Whiteley can enhance her chances
Orbital Chime caught stewards' attention last time for not trying - watch for any similar riding tactics

races.name: Remembrance Of Ferdinand Addo Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB)

runners_data.name: Constant Star
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter returning from 30-day break with solid second last time, Morris booking suggests confidence despite Clover's poor recent record

runners_data.name: Imelda
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity for in-form Loughnane stable with Lewis Edmunds taking the ride, dangerous wildcard given her unraced status

runners_data.name: Thai Princess
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from powerful Balding yard with Probert booked, disappointed on debut but breeding suggests improvement likely

runners_data.name: Rogue Desire
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 233-day absence, showed promise in defeat at this track and distance on similar going

runners_data.name: Thimble
runners_data.note: Held-up runner with consistent style, 45 days since last run but showed glimpses of ability in maidens at this level

runners_data.name: Action Reaction
runners_data.note: Back-of-field runner with poor recent form for Boughey, quick return suggests connections seeking easier opportunity

runners_data.name: Safe Zone
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid RPR figures, 40-day break with Mitchell booking indicates stable confidence in this grade

runners_data.name: Difford Girl
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse carrying significant weight penalty, low OR suggests she's outclassed but track-and-trip proven

races.paceDynamic: Constant Star will likely set the pace from stall rise with no other confirmed front runners in this field of eight fillies. The modest early gallop should be sustainable given the lack of pace pressure, creating a steady rhythm through the first half of this 7f contest. The hold-up horses — Rogue Desire, Thimble, Action Reaction, Safe Zone, and Difford Girl — will be content to track behind in the early stages. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the modest pace will compress the field and create a tactical finish where those with late speed can strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Constant Star sets a steady, uncontested pace as expected
scenarios.body: The field stays bunched and the finish becomes a sprint where the fresher hold-up horses can unleash their turn of foot. Rogue Desire and Safe Zone are best positioned to capitalize with their proven ability to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes more genuinely run than expected with early pressure
scenarios.body: Constant Star's stamina comes into play and those tracking close behind can kick clear before the hold-up horses get into gear. Thai Princess could benefit from her Balding training and Probert booking despite modest debut form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly raced improver strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Imelda shows significant improvement from her unraced status under Loughnane
scenarios.body: The David Loughnane-trained filly could have natural ability that hasn't been exposed yet, capitalizing on the modest pace to spring a surprise. Her unknown running style provides tactical flexibility that experienced rivals lack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot gets competitive
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace allows weaker horses to stay closer than usual
scenarios.body: Difford Girl or Action Reaction could outrun their recent poor form in this restricted company, though their ceiling remains limited. The tactical nature of the race might mask class differences temporarily.

watchPoints.text: Watch for any early pace pressure on Constant Star which could change the entire complexion and favor those tracking closer
Monitor Imelda's market moves as any strong support would suggest Loughnane expects significant improvement from debut
Check if Thai Princess settles better than on debut as Probert's booking suggests Balding expects a step forward
Watch Action Reaction's early position as her poor recent form suggests she needs everything to fall right tactically
Observe Safe Zone's finishing kick as her consistent RPR suggests she could be competitive if getting the right pace setup

races.name: Thank You Opus Foundation Handicap

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong recent form for in-form Richard Hannon stable, Joe Leavy booking suggests confidence after just 8 days break

runners_data.name: Kirkdale
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 78-day break for Edward Bethell, consistent at this trip but freshness question remains

runners_data.name: Lequinto
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with excellent course record, 3 wins from similar going conditions for Tony Carroll

runners_data.name: Pianoforte
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing cheekpieces, Julie Camacho's 0/5 recent record is concerning despite horse's solid RPR

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with tactical speed, key pace angle for John O'Shea after 18-day freshen-up

runners_data.name: Brian The Snail
runners_data.note: 12-year-old hold-up specialist with solid course form, wearing cheekpieces for Patrick Morris

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with first-time tongue-tie for Michael Appleby, low weight advantage but inconsistent recent form

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with course-and-distance win, Charlie Wallis 0/3 recent record but Rob Hornby booking is positive

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying first-time hood, ear-plugs and blinkers for Scott Dixon, Spotlight flags concerns about revival
runners_data.comment: Tumbling down the weights but showing no sign of taking advantage
runners_data.spotlight: Went the wrong way for George Boughey last year and no sign of a revival for new yard this winter.

races.paceDynamic: Due Date and Punchbowl Flyer will clash for the early lead in this competitive handicap, with both confirmed front-runners likely to engage from the off. Their battle should create an honest gallop over this sharp 6f trip, stretching the field and setting up a genuine pace. The remaining seven runners all adopt hold-up tactics, meaning they'll be relying on the two leaders to do the donkey work before swooping late. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the pace is genuine and the field will be strung out, allowing closers to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong pace benefits closers
scenarios.trigger: If Due Date and Punchbowl Flyer engage in a sustained battle from the gates
scenarios.body: The two leaders will set a fierce gallop that plays into the hands of the seven hold-up horses behind. The pace will be unsustainable and allow the strongest finishers to sweep past in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One leader dominates uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If either Due Date or Punchbowl Flyer gets an uncontested lead while the other fails to fire
scenarios.body: The lone leader will dictate terms and potentially steal a march on the hold-up brigade. This tactical advantage could prove decisive if they can maintain their kick to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers fail to quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by a moderate early pace or fail to find gaps
scenarios.body: The seven runners tracking behind may find themselves in trouble if the pace isn't strong enough or if traffic problems emerge. A tactical race could favour those who race closer to the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise prominent runner emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the supposed hold-up horses breaks character and races more prominently than expected
scenarios.body: A change of tactics from the likes of Valsharah or Kirkdale could catch the field off-guard. This would further complicate the pace dynamics and create new race flow.

watchPoints.text: Due Date and Punchbowl Flyer must both break alertly — if one misses the start the entire pace dynamic collapses
Valsharah applies tongue-tie for first time which could spark improvement for Michael Appleby
Cayman Tai represents the strongest recent form with Richard Hannon's 4/24 strike-rate backing up the selection
Brian The Snail's 12-year-old legs may struggle to quicken from his hold-up position despite consistent course form
Kirkdale returns from 78-day absence — watch market confidence as Edward Bethell has been selective with runners recently

races.name: Thank You To Omari For The Support Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Charmaine
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from six-month break under Daniel Muscutt, but James Fanshawe is in good form and her previous win came after a similar layoff.
runners_data.comment: Looked to find this mark beyond her after two wins last spring but this less competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Novice win as a 3yo came after four months off, which is a positive as she returns from a six-month absence; looked to find this sort of mark just beyond her after two victories last spring (Tapeta, Polytrack) but this is less competitive.

runners_data.name: Maasai Mara
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for in-form John O'Shea but has been disappointing in recent starts and faces a significant step back up in distance.

runners_data.name: Codiak
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with two recent wins, Edward Bethell's strike-rate is modest but Callum Rodriguez takes over from the claimer.

runners_data.name: Polling Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran returning from seven-month break for Bernard Llewellyn whose yard is struggling, though David Probert's booking suggests some confidence.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Donegal
runners_data.note: The only confirmed leader with good recent form, Billy Loughnane will look to steal a march but Charlie Johnston's strike-rate is concerning.

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from long break carrying bottom weight but Bernard Llewellyn's poor recent record is a significant negative.

runners_data.name: Gemmari
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good form for Richard Hannon whose yard is flying, Joe Leavy rides and the recent Lingfield win suggests he handles this trip well.

races.paceDynamic: Pride Of Donegal will lead from the start with only Bulldog Spirit likely to race prominently, creating a very soft early pace in this small field of seven. The hold-up horses - Charmaine, Maasai Mara, Codiak, Polling Day and Gemmari - will be bunched together in behind, meaning the pace will be pedestrian for most of the journey. With such a modest gallop likely, this race will become a sprint finish where tactical positioning and a strong turn of foot will be crucial. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks - the lack of early pace means the field will finish in a bunch and those with the best acceleration will prevail.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate finish
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Donegal sets a steady pace without pressure from Bulldog Spirit.
scenarios.body: The field arrives at the home turn in a tight group, setting up a furious sprint finish where horses with proven finishing kicks and good recent form can strike. Form horses like Codiak and Gemmari, who both have strong closing sectionals, will thrive in this tactical battle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner steals march
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Donegal quickens turning for home while the hold-up horses are still organising.
scenarios.body: Billy Loughnane times his move perfectly on the leader, getting first run on rivals who are caught flat-footed by the change of pace. The held-up brigade launch their challenges too late as Pride Of Donegal has stolen a decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Outsider strikes from rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stop-start and allows a horse returning from a break to produce a telling late burst.
scenarios.body: The modest early gallop suits a fresh horse who can unleash one powerful finishing effort when others have used their energy in position. Charmaine, despite her long absence, could benefit from James Fanshawe's patient approach and Daniel Muscutt's timing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Pride Of Donegal and Bulldog Spirit go too slowly and create a messy, stop-start gallop.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a complete lottery with horses getting in each other's way and jockeyship becoming paramount. Any horse getting a clear run at the right moment could capitalise on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Pride Of Donegal sets too strong a pace early - if Billy Loughnane gets competitive with Bulldog Spirit, the leader could empty out.
Codiak's jumping from the handicapper after two wins - the 4lb rise may have found his limit despite his excellent current form.
Charmaine's market support - any confidence in the betting suggests James Fanshawe expects her to reproduce her best form fresh.
Bulldog Spirit's fitness after 210 days off - Sean Bowen will need to judge the pace perfectly as the stable is badly out of form.
Gemmari's tactical position - Joe Leavy must avoid getting trapped behind horses in the straight given the likely bunched finish.

races.name: Founding Member Of ACCI WRPA Handicap

runners_data.name: Beaming Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs strong pace over this minimum trip, returning from just 10 days with David Loughnane's stable in poor recent form

runners_data.name: Blue Force
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid 5f record, Sean Bowen booking suggests confidence despite Antony Brittain's modest strike rate

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Returns after 177-day absence but has shown good course form previously, prominent style could work if race sets up right

runners_data.name: Candy Warhol
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner carrying just 128lbs, Scott Dixon stable in decent form with 2/24 recent record and reliable over course and distance

runners_data.name: Phoenix Beach
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from in-form Scott Dixon yard, second string but could benefit if stablemate Candy Warhol sets it up perfectly

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Reliable course winner who excels over 5f, Rob Hornby booking and Charlie Wallis stable confidence evident from recent wins here

runners_data.name: Amerjeet
runners_data.note: Drops back to preferred 5f trip with Hollie Doyle aboard, best form has come at this distance despite 0/4 course record

runners_data.name: Toomuchforme
runners_data.note: Bounced back with visor fitted last time, gets 3lb apprentice allowance and Antony Brittain double-handed suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: Revived by visor on last two starts, beating Shalaa Asker at Southwell last month; solid
runners_data.spotlight: Revived by a visor of late, third at Newcastle in February and then getting the better of Shalaa Asker at Southwell 25 days ago; 3lb higher today and the stable also runs Blue Force.

races.paceDynamic: Candy Warhol will take this field along from the front with Blue Force, Betweenthesticks and Toomuchforme settling prominently behind. The pace should be honest but not breakneck over this minimum trip, with the front-running Candy Warhol able to dictate terms without severe pressure from the prominent racers. The large contingent of hold-up horses (Beaming Light, Shalaa Asker, Phoenix Beach, Amerjeet) will be relying on the pace being strong enough to come from off the speed. This setup moderately favours prominent racers and strong finishers — the pace will be genuine enough to create opportunities but not so fierce as to guarantee a closer's race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Candy Warhol gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The 7-year-old can use his 5lb weight advantage and front-running style to steal a march on closers who need stronger pace. Phoenix Beach from the same stable could pick up the pieces if the leader falters late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest enough to set up the race for closers
scenarios.body: Shalaa Asker's recent course wins and Rob Hornby booking suggest stable confidence, while Amerjeet drops back to 5f where she's shown her best form. The pace should be sufficient to bring these into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Force or Toomuchforme can track the leader and pounce late
scenarios.body: Blue Force has solid 5f form and Sean Bowen's booking adds confidence, while Toomuchforme bounced back to form with visor fitted last time. Both can sit handy and strike when the pace tells.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the market leaders underperform
scenarios.body: Betweenthesticks returns after 177 days but has course form and could outrun odds if the break has freshened her up. Phoenix Beach at bigger odds could benefit from stable confidence with Scott Dixon running two.

watchPoints.text: Candy Warhol if getting soft early fractions - the lone leader could steal a march with his 7lb weight advantage over main rivals
Toomuchforme's visor impact - fitted for first time at Southwell when winning, could be the key to another improved effort
Scott Dixon's double-handed approach with Candy Warhol and Phoenix Beach - suggests stable expects one to run well
Shalaa Asker's Rob Hornby booking - top jockey rarely rides for Charlie Wallis, suggests stable confidence in 8-year-old's chances
Blue Force and Betweenthesticks both representing Antony Brittain stable - 1/12 recent record suggests low confidence despite double entry

races.name: Thank You, Ina Deans Lifelong Carer Handicap

runners_data.name: Karakula Dancer
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with excellent recent form (2-1-1-2-3) and strong going record on similar conditions, representing in-form Ferguson stable

runners_data.name: Panthere Noir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse getting 10lbs weight relief with inexperienced 5lb claimer, trained by Russell/Scudamore partnership whose recent form is patchy

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who won last time and gets tactical advantage with uncontested lead, though carries top weight for Botti who has decent strike rate

runners_data.name: Zoustellar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back up in trip for in-form Boughey, showed improved effort when fourth last time but needs to find more

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Express is the sole confirmed front runner and will face no early pressure, allowing him to dictate terms from the front at his own tempo. The remaining five runners are all hold-up horses who will settle behind and look to finish strongly. This creates a perfect scenario for the pace-setter to steal a march, as the hold-up brigade may leave themselves too much to do if they don't position early enough. This setup strongly favours prominent/leading horses — with no pace pressure, Lexington Express can control the race and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still organising their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lexington Express Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express gets an uncontested lead and maintains a steady gallop
scenarios.body: He can dictate ideal fractions and have enough left to resist the late charge from the hold-up horses. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Coordinate
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses position closer and launch coordinated challenges
scenarios.body: The sustained late pressure could overwhelm Lexington Express despite his tactical advantage. Karakula Dancer's recent winning form and strong going record make him the likely beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Early Pace Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express goes too slow early and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the hold-up horses' natural finishing kick gives them the edge. Amazing Anita could benefit from the strongest late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express struggles with the distance or weight and fades early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with no clear pace, potentially suiting an improver like Panthere Noir who gets significant weight relief. The field would come home in a bunch.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Express must be watched for any signs of struggling with the sustained gallop - if he shortens his stride approaching the furlong pole, the hold-up horses will pounce
Monitor how quickly the hold-up horses position themselves turning for home - if they're all still last with two furlongs to run, they may have left too much to do
Watch Karakula Dancer's position at halfway - his recent form suggests he needs to be handy to deliver his finishing kick effectively
Check if Amazing Anita looks rusty early after her month off - any tardiness leaving the stalls could prove costly in a small field
Observe whether Panthere Noir's inexperienced rider can get her into a rhythm early - the 5lb claimer needs to avoid getting caught wide
